releases.notes:
**Requires Minecraft 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, and [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api).**

Download `primordia-2.15.3-26.2.jar` below and drop it into your `mods` folder alongside Fabric API. That's the whole install. See the [README](https://github.com/Zeyphers/Primordia#install) if you'd like it spelled out.

---

## Splicing: take something from the animals you study

Until now the payoff for studying a species to *Complete* was a better-worded paragraph in the field guide. Now a decoded genome is something you can become.

Build a **Splicing Bench** (a Basic Gene Lab, a diamond, iron, glass and redstone), choose a lineage you've fully decoded, and the bench isolates one block of its genome into a **Trait Serum**. Isolating costs a heart. Drink the serum and the block is yours.

There are six branches: **Physiology, Disposition, Climate, Colour, Light and Habit**. The tree is authored and nothing in it is. A node gives you permission to carry a kind of trait up to a strength, and what you actually get is the donor's own value:

- **Potency is the donor's real value.** A lineage that has spent forty generations being chased across open ground gives you real speed; a sedentary one gives you almost nothing. Each branch in the field guide names the best donor you have on file, so it's worth going back out to find a better one.
- **You take the linkage block, not the gene.** You get the whole contiguous span of the donor's genome, whatever else that animal happens to be. The screen shows every trait in the block, costs included, before you commit.
- **Depth is earned by finding better examples.** Each branch opens at *Trace* and deepens to *Expressed* and *Dominant* as you decode more lineages that carry the trait strongly. Nothing is bought; a trait the ecology rarely produces is simply slow to unlock.
- **Slots force a choice.** Two to start, plus one for every branch taken to Dominant, up to five. Reverting is free but happens at the bench, so you can't re-spec halfway down a cave.

A **Light** splice makes you glow in the donor's colour from the parts it lit, and with LambDynamicLights installed you light the cave around you. The field guide's new **Self** tab is an anatomy plate of your own character, turning to follow the cursor, with a card and a leader line from each branch to the part of the body it changes.

The design and its reasoning are in [`MD/SPLICING.md`](https://github.com/Zeyphers/Primordia/blob/main/MD/SPLICING.md).

## Legs no longer walk through each other

Front knees used to bend backward and hind knees forward. That's true of the elbow and stifle hidden inside a real animal's body, but it's wrong for the joints you actually see, the carpus and hock, which point the other way. Drawn that way, a quadruped's knees aimed at each other across its belly, and at the end of every stride the front foot trailing back met the hind foot reaching forward. **Measured over a flat walk, same-side legs passed through each other on 60% of a saurian's frames** and a third of a pack hunter's.

Two changes close it:

- **Every knee now points away from the middle of the body.** Front legs bend forward, hind legs bend back, the same rule six- and eight-legged creatures already followed. Bipeds stand on their hindlimbs, so their knees now face forward, with the hock bending back behind on three-bone legs. Their only pair used to be classified as forelimbs, which bent the knee backward and folded the hock in toward the other leg.
- **A stride can no longer carry one foot into the next.** The gait sized its stride from each leg's reach and never asked about the leg in front of it. It now caps the stride by the gap to the next foot on the same side, charged only for the approach that pair's gait phase actually produces.

releases.notes:
**Requires Minecraft 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, and [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api).**

Download `primordia-2.5.0-26.2.jar` below and drop it into your `mods` folder alongside Fabric API. That's the whole install — see the [README](https://github.com/Zeyphers/Primordia#install) if you'd like it spelled out.

---

## Creatures no longer sound like one animal with two knobs

Every timbre parameter used to come straight off the genome, continuously, which sounds like the right approach and is not. Measured across 4400 voices, **nine of those parameters correlated with `AGGRESSION` at |r| between 0.56 and 0.95** — open quotient, chaos, shimmer, jitter, spectral tilt and the rest. The entire roughness character of a voice was one gene. Two principal components accounted for 68% of all variation, and those two were, in effect, size and temper: every creature sat somewhere between a big calm one and a small cross one, and once you had heard both corners you had heard the range.

Widening each parameter's range cannot fix that — it stretches the sheet without adding a dimension to it. **Voice families** add the missing one. A family is a mechanism rather than a preset: real animals do not differ by having the same throat turned up louder, they differ by making sound in structurally different ways. A whistle is not a quiet roar. Families are chosen by nearest prototype in trait space, so none of them can win simply by having more terms in its score — the first attempt summed weighted terms and put 78% of the population into three of eight families.

## Legs stopped trailing behind the body

A foot's plant is chosen when it lifts and reached when it lands, and the body travels the whole swing in between. The gait led each plant by half the stance travel, which is only symmetric if the foot arrives the instant it leaves — so at a duty factor of 0.62 every foot touched down *already* behind its hip and then fell a full stance further back.

Measured across every archetype over seven terrains: **0.29 of a leg length aft, on every leg**. Nothing caught it, because reach, cadence, contact quality and body attitude were all correct the whole time — there is no reading of "is the leg overstretched" that notices an animal being dragged along by its shoulders. Including the swing's own travel in the lead brings it to 0.13 overall and 0.06 at a walk, and quietly improves over-reach and foot-sinking as well.

The whole gait now sizes itself from each leg's real reach envelope, and `gradle gaitReport` walks all eleven archetypes over block terrain to measure it.

## Every creature is built from the same size of block

Voxel mode snaps the mesh to a lattice that is a power-of-two multiple of the base voxel, so a grid even one per cent coarser than a pixel is not one per cent coarser on screen — it is rounded to two pixels. Resolution was only ever raised for thin limbs, so the animals that landed there were the ones asking for nothing: **large, thick-legged creatures came out visibly blockier than whatever was standing next to them**. It was 0.2% of the population, which is rare enough to look like a rendering fault and impossible to miss side by side.

## Ornament no longer follows the legs

A frill hangs off a spine bone but can sit, in bind pose, right beside a thigh — so the thigh was the nearest bone, "owned" that vertex, and drove it. Standing still it looks fine; the moment the animal walks, the veil stretches toward the swinging limb.

Measured before the fix: **26% of every frill vertex the generator makes was driven by a leg bone**, at up to 0.98 weight, along with 7% of ears and a scatter of plates, horns and light organs. A limb now drives limbs and its own group and nothing else. `gradle skinProbe` prints the split by surface and every ornament row reads zero.

releases.notes:
**Requires Minecraft 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, and [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api).**

Download `primordia-2.0.1-26.2.jar` below and drop it into your `mods` folder alongside Fabric API. That's the whole install — see the [README](https://github.com/Zeyphers/Primordia#install) if you'd like it spelled out.

---

## The family tree reads as a window now

The Bloodlines tab is a viewport that pans, and it used to end at a hard edge — branches and boxes sliced off mid-stroke at the boundary, which reads as a rendering fault rather than as a drawing that continues past the page. The outer 14 pixels of each edge now fade back into the paper.

Two things had to be right for that to look like anything. The falloff is a **smoothstep** rather than a power curve: a quadratic is already at half coverage three pixels in, so its whole transition happens inside a band too narrow to see and the result is the same hard cutoff, just moved inward. And the wash is the **page texture re-blitted over itself**, not a flat fill of the page colour — that constant is lighter than most of the sheet, so filling with it put a white halo around the tab and painted over the grain and stains the texture carries.

## The tree can no longer be dragged off the page

The same viewport had no travel limit, so it could be flung into empty paper with nothing on screen to say which way the tree went. The only recovery was to change tab and come back.

The pan is now held inside the tree's own extents, with the rule "the tree may leave the page until one whole box is left". The limit is derived from the layout rather than fixed, so it **grows with the collection on its own** — a two-node tree gets a few pixels of travel, a fifty-node one gets most of a screen in every direction. Zoom is in the same arithmetic, so pulling back to see a whole clade widens the leash at the same time as it shrinks the drawing.

## `/primordia editor` no longer needs cheats

The editor is a modelling tool: it bakes meshes from genomes typed into a web page, and it can neither read your save nor write to it. Gating it behind cheats meant the one command a player might actually want was the one they could not reach.

Every other command still needs gamemaster permissions. The editor binds to `127.0.0.1`, so on a dedicated server the page is only reachable from the machine hosting it.

## `/primordia debug lava`

For testing what the ecology does with a sudden hole in it — carcass handling, the region ledger's response to a lineage crashing, scavengers arriving. Sends every creature within 200 blocks (or a radius you name) walking into the nearest **exposed** lava; buried lava is unreachable however near it is.

Doing it by pathfinding rather than by `/kill` is the point: what is being tested is the dying, not the deaths.

mods.name: Primordia
mods.description: Procedurally generated, evolving creatures. Genomes grow skeletons, skeletons grow SDF bodies, bodies walk with IK, and populations evolve and reshape the world.

releases.notes:
**Requires Minecraft 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, and [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api).**

Download `primordia-2.0.0-26.2.jar` below and drop it into your `mods` folder alongside Fabric API. That's the whole install — see the [README](https://github.com/Zeyphers/Primordia#install) if you'd like it spelled out.

---

## Creatures have their own voices

Every call is **synthesised from the animal's own anatomy** — pitch from body mass, timbre from the length of its head and neck, growl from aggression. Nothing borrows a vanilla animal's sound any more.

The interesting part is the roughness. A clean source-and-filter model sounds like an organ, because a perfectly periodic source through a fixed filter *is* an organ. Real vertebrate calls are pervaded by four irregularities — deterministic chaos, subharmonics, biphonation, and frequency jumps — and those carry most of the impression that something alive is making the sound. All four are modelled.

There's a new **Creature voices** section in the settings if you want them quieter, or off.

## You will meet far more kinds of creature

The generator has always been able to produce around a thousand different combinations of horns, ears, tails and eyes. It was producing about fifteen of them.

Every gene the body plans don't constrain was drawn toward the middle of its range — and those are exactly the genes that decide what a creature's *face* looks like. So every animal had a mid-length muzzle, mid-sized ears, mid-length horns. They differed on paper and looked the same.

That's rebuilt. Some numbers, measured over 5,000 generated creatures:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Ornament strength | 0.139 | **0.251** |
| How unlike its closest twin a creature is | 0.653 | **1.101** |
| Casque horns | 0.4% | **8.1%** |
| Plain eyes | 1.5% | **13.2%** |
| Fanned ears | 1.0% | **14.3%** |

Siblings in a herd now differ in horns and markings while sharing a body plan, which is what real intraspecific variation looks like.

## Places have their own animals

Body plans are now chosen from **the climate and the job** — so a desert's grazers aren't a rainforest's, and a creature's shape tells you what it eats. Previously a region's grazer could be built on the apex predator's skeleton with its diet quietly overridden.

A desert herbivore is usually a sprinter; a rainforest one is usually a long-necked browser. Tundra rarely supports a large predator at all.

## Also

- **Feet** — hooves, pads, splayed toes, talons, webbing, chitin tips.
- **Creatures stand up to four blocks tall**, rather than everything large being squashed to the same 2.5.

## Fixes

- **Holes in creature bodies at the hips.** 26% of creatures had at least one; now none.
- **Ornament dragged by leg bones** — over a third of frill, plate and spine vertices were following a nearby leg, so a creature's veil rippled when it walked.
- **Shading on crouching creatures.** Faces turned inside out by a deep crouch were lit from behind.
- **Arms growing through legs** on anything with more than two legs. Only bipeds have arms now.
- **Wading.** A two-block-tall creature stepping into an ankle-deep stream started swimming, because Minecraft uses the same fluid depth for every mob regardless of size. It's measured against the creature's own eye height now — if its head is above water, it walks.
- The Sample Cooler now faces the right way when you place it.

---

**Upgrading from 1.x:** existing worlds are safe. Creatures you already have keep the bodies they were generated with; the new variety appears in land you haven't explored yet.

releases.notes:
**Fixes a crash introduced in 1.8.4.** If you ran `/primordia editor`, quitting Minecraft afterwards would hang and the shutdown watchdog would kill the process with a crash report. Update from 1.8.4.

## What happened

`HttpServer` creates its listener thread itself and does not mark it a daemon, and `setExecutor` does not reach it — that only covers the handler pool, whose thread *was* already a daemon and duly idle. So once the editor had been started, one non-daemon thread outlived the game window and the JVM never exited.

In the crash report's thread dump, `HTTP-Dispatcher` was the only non-daemon thread left besides `DestroyJavaVM`.

A JVM shutdown hook cannot fix this, because the JVM never *begins* shutting down while a non-daemon thread is alive. The server has to be stopped from Minecraft's own lifecycle, which it now is:

- `CLIENT_STOPPING` on quitting the game — the case that actually bit
- `SERVER_STOPPING` for dedicated servers, gated on `isDedicatedServer` so that leaving a world for the main menu does not close the editor out from under you

Everything in [1.8.4](https://github.com/Zeyphers/Primordia/releases/tag/v1.8.4-26.2) is otherwise unchanged.

mods.name: Primordia
mods.description: Procedurally generated, evolving creatures. Genomes grow skeletons, skeletons grow SDF bodies, bodies walk with IK, and populations evolve and reshape the world.

releases.notes:
> ⚠️ **Superseded by [1.8.5](https://github.com/Zeyphers/Primordia/releases/tag/v1.8.5-26.2).** Running `/primordia editor` in this version leaves an HTTP thread alive that prevents Minecraft from exiting, so quitting crashes with a watchdog report. Please use 1.8.5.

Requires **Minecraft 26.2** and Fabric Loader.

## Creatures now spawn far from spawn

Fly a few hundred blocks out and creatures stopped appearing. `RegionMaterialiser.place` passed chunk coordinates to `hasChunkAt`, which takes **block** coordinates and shifts them down itself — so every one of its 64 probes asked about chunk `x >> 8` instead of `x >> 4`.

The two agree at the origin and diverge linearly with distance, so past a few hundred blocks the probe landed nowhere near the player, all 64 chunks came back unloaded, and the region materialised nothing at all.

| region blockX | probed blockX | gap |
|---|---|---|
| 128 | 0 | 128 |
| 2048 | 128 | 1920 |
| 999936 | 62496 | 937440 |

Confirmed fixed in game.

## `/primordia editor`

A browser-based creature editor, served from the game itself. It runs the **real** generator — body plan, signed distance field, extraction, vertex colours, skin weights, and the actual `CreatureAnimator` walk cycle — and the page only rasterises what Java produced, so it cannot drift from what the game draws.

- Voxel and smooth modes, LOD tiers, sharp shading and flat face colour, all matching the game's own settings
- All 88 genes as live sliders
- Drag any joint and the server solves for the genome that puts it there, preferring loci that move that joint and little else
- Model / Rig / Debug views, including an overlay for faces that weld two limbs together
- Copy the genome code and spawn it with `/primordia spawn code <genome>` — a designed creature is an ordinary member of the population and breeds with the wild one

The command replies with a clickable link rather than launching a browser, since a command runs on the server. The editor is inert until you run it and binds `127.0.0.1` only.

## Creatures are easier to hit

Minecraft gives an entity one bounding box and uses it for collision, pushing, suffocation, pathfinding and hit detection at once, which forces a compromise on a body that is nothing like a box.

Creatures now carry a **second hitbox on the spine that exists only to register hits**. It is handed to the hit scan and nothing else, so it clips through terrain and mobs and moves nothing. It tracks the live posed skeleton, so it follows the body as it bobs and leans. Visible under F3+B in red.

A creature also now shadows the block behind it — you can no longer mine through one.

**Primary hitboxes are shorter.** Seven of the eleven archetypes had a box taller than the creature inside it, worst on short-legged ones where the old floor made a cave crawler's box 25% taller than the animal. Every archetype now sits at or under its own silhouette.

## Also

- Limbs fair into the body instead of butting against it — the trunk-to-limb join was a hard union, leaving a crease around every shoulder and hip
- A vertex can no longer be skinned to two different limbs, which was dragging spider toes together and stretching a face between them
